-122.56000,38.09730.name: Lane Fertility Institute
-122.56000,38.09730.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Danielle E. Lane, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-72.97128,45.61976.status: Probationary Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, April 2024
-72.97128,45.61976.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Probationary Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, April 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-79.38553,43.65060.name: The Centre for Phenogenomics
-79.38553,43.65060.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, January 2024
-79.38553,43.65060.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, January 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. -2.01000,48.65000.name: Groupe Roullier / seed & input distribution
-2.01000,48.65000.desc: A large French group in fertiliser, animal nutrition and seed distribution, privately held and little discussed outside the sector. Distribution is where a farmer’s actual choice is made: whatever is bred anywhere, what reaches a field is what the local distributor stocks, and that decision is taken by companies almost nobody outside farming can name.

70.80000,22.31000.name: Bt cotton found growing before any approval existed
70.80000,22.31000.type: Cotton, unapproved trait in commercial fields
70.80000,22.31000.size: Estimated tens of thousands of hectares before approval
70.80000,22.31000.desc: Bt cotton was found growing in Gujarat before India had approved any engineered crop, and the government had to decide retroactively what to do with a harvest already in the market. It chose to approve.

-82.15000,22.99000.name: Instituto Nacional de Ciencias Agrícolas
-82.15000,22.99000.state: San José de las Lajas, Mayabeque
-82.15000,22.99000.desc: Cuba’s agricultural research institute, in a country that turned to low-input and biological methods after Soviet fertiliser and fuel supplies ended in 1990. That transition is the largest involuntary experiment in low-input agriculture anyone has run, and its results are argued over by both sides of this debate.

-86.53330,16.31670.name: Minicircle
-86.53330,16.31670.desc: Sells a follistatin gene therapy intended to increase muscle mass, offered in Hondurás at Próspera, a special economic zone chosen because it regulates medicine on its own terms. Not approved anywhere with a conventional regulator. It is the clearest existing case of enhancement rather than treatment, sold to people who are not ill, in a jurisdiction selected for permitting it.

-84.32600,33.79900.name: Federal Select Agent Program
-84.32600,33.79900.desc: Registers every US laboratory permitted to hold the pathogens and toxins judged most dangerous, inspects them, and can bar individuals from access. It is one of very few mechanisms in the world that decides in advance that particular biological work may not be done — and its list is where the boundary is actually drawn between research and a weapon.

34.79900,31.92800.name: ADAMA
34.79900,31.92800.desc: A large off-patent crop protection company, Chinese-owned through ChemChina, selling the generics that follow once a herbicide's patent expires. Generic competition is what makes a tolerance trait cheap to use, so it shapes adoption as much as the trait's own licensing does.
